<pr_description>
Consider the following PR description:
UserCreationForm should save data from ManyToMany form fields
Description
	
When using contrib.auth.forms.UserCreationForm with a custom User model which has ManyToManyField fields, the data in all related form fields (e.g. a ModelMultipleChoiceField) is not saved. 
This is because unlike its parent class django.forms.ModelForm, UserCreationForm.save(commit=True) omits to call self.save_m2m(). 
This has been discussed on the #django-developers mailing list ​https://groups.google.com/u/1/g/django-developers/c/2jj-ecoBwE4 and I'm ready to work on a PR.

</pr_description>

The issue is clear: in the `save` method, when `commit=True`, it calls `super().save(commit=False)` and then `user.save()`, but never calls `self.save_m2m()`. The parent `ModelForm.save()` with `commit=True` would normally handle M2M saving, but since `UserCreationForm` always calls `super().save(commit=False)`, it needs to explicitly call `self.save_m2m()`.

def save(self, commit=True):
        """
        Save this form's self.instance object if commit=True. Otherwise, add
        a save_m2m() method to the form which can be called after the instance
        is saved manually at a later time. Return the model instance.
        """
        if self.errors:
            raise ValueError(
                "The %s could not be %s because the data didn't validate."
                % (
                    self.instance._meta.object_name,
                    "created" if self.instance._state.adding else "changed",
                )
            )
        if commit:
            # If committing, save the instance and the m2m data immediately.
            self.instance.save()
            self._save_m2m()
        else:
            # If not committing, add a method to the form to allow deferred
            # saving of m2m data.
            self.save_m2m = self._save_m2m
        return self.instance
